name: Louisiana
status_why: The Voter Portal's JSON files answered scripts; folder 20261103 is posted.
system: State-built: the Louisiana Secretary of State's 'Graphical election results' on the Voter Portal (an app whose data are JSON files served through one Data?blob= endpoint). Louisiana runs every election in the state, parish offices included, through this one system.

results_page.label: Louisiana Secretary of State: election results

feeds.address: https://voterportal.sos.la.gov/ElectionResults/ElectionResults/Data?blob=ElectionDates.htm (list of elections with PKElectionID and ResultsOfficial 0/1); then Data?blob=<yyyymmdd>/ElectionRaces.htm (every race, with RaceID and Level), <yyyymmdd>/RacesCandidates_Multiparish.htm and <yyyymmdd>/Votes_Multiparish.htm (statewide votes for multi-parish races)
feeds.updates: Rewritten as parishes report on election night (the Votes files are the moving part); the app polls them. Exact interval not stated.
feeds.note: 200 on 2026-10-09 for ElectionDates.htm (91 KB JSON; DefaultElectionDate 11/03/2026, PKElectionID 344, ResultsOfficial 0) and for 20261103/ElectionRaces.htm (103 KB; U.S. Senator RaceID 67997, U.S. Representative 1st District RaceID 70195, ...). The .htm names hold JSON.

feeds.address: Same files: Levels 140 (U.S. Senator) and 145 (U.S. Representative) in <yyyymmdd>/ElectionRaces.htm; votes in Votes_Multiparish.htm
feeds.note: Nov 3 2026: the House contest is an open primary (runoff Dec 12, 2026, folder 20261212); the Senate has a regular general. Votes records carry AbsenteeExpected and AbsenteeReporting (la.py line 239).

feeds.address: Data?blob=<yyyymmdd>/RacesCandidates/ByParish_<01..64>.htm (races in each parish) and the parish vote files beside them; csv/ByParish_<race>.csv gives one race's votes by parish
feeds.note: The kit's state_local_la.py already reads the Nov 3 ByParish race files (cached as ballot_cache/la/local/sl_la_2026_local_results_feed.json). Parish vote file names for election night were not requested today.

feeds.address: The graphical site offers precinct views; the file name was not checked
feeds.note: Precinct-level files after the election are on the Secretary's 'Post-election statistics' (PostElectionStatsAvailable flag in ElectionDates.htm).

races_in_feed: Everything on the ballot in Louisiana: Senate, House (open primary), Public Service Commission, judges, parish and municipal offices, school boards, constitutional amendments and local propositions (levels 998 and 999).
local: No: parishes do not run their own results sites; every parish race is in the Secretary's feed.
how_counted: Parishes report through the night. The House contest is an open primary: if no one wins a majority, the top two meet on December 12.
count_order: Vote records carry AbsenteeExpected and AbsenteeReporting.
vote_types: Partly: the vote records carry absentee reporting counts (AbsenteeExpected, AbsenteeReporting), so early and mail ballots can be told apart from precincts in the reporting status; whether votes are split by type in the election-night files is to be checked on the 2024 replay.

rules.note: A majority wins; otherwise the top two go to the Dec 12 runoff.

rules.applies: U.S. Senate (general after closed party primaries)
state and local offices on Nov 3

certify.rule: Within 30 days after the election (La. Rev. Stat. 18:513).
certify.local_rule: Returns to the clerk of court by 4 p.m. on the fifth day (La. Rev. Stat. 18:574).
certify.source: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself

terms: None stated on the data files.
scout_blocked: Nothing refused scripts. The Candidate Inquiry pages on the same host also answer scripts.
scout_plan: Louisiana is the easiest state in this group: one host, JSON files, every level from the Senate to a parish school board. On election night the updater reads ElectionDates.htm once, then Votes_Multiparish.htm and the parish vote files for 20261103 every few minutes, maps RaceIDs to the races state_local_la.py already loaded, and marks every figure unofficial until ElectionDates.htm turns ResultsOfficial to 1. Rehearse on the 20241105 folder. Remember the House contest is an open primary with a Dec 12 runoff, so 'winner' on Nov 3 often means 'advances to the runoff'.
notes: The three Supreme Court and four Court of Appeal seats on the ballot lists had one qualified candidate each and are elected unopposed; they are not in the results files.
sources: NCSL, 'Election Certification Deadlines' (www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/certification-deadlines), read 2026-10-10; secondary: a summary of each state's law, not the law itself
